beats.title: World
beats.headline: Vatican City: Pope at Gemelli; Bulgaria drones; NK follow-up.
beats.body:
Vatican City. Pope Leo XIV was admitted Tuesday morning to Rome’s Gemelli Hospital for afternoon surgery to remove a “small, localized lung nodule” found in routine checks—his first hospitalization of the pontificate. He walked in and waved to well-wishers; thoracic surgeon Prof. Stefano Margaritora leads the team, with a roughly one-week stay expected and audiences canceled through Oct. 20. Cardinal Tagle still presides Wednesday’s Amoris Laetitia closing Mass; the synthesis waits for the Pope’s review.

Africa. The UN Security Council meets today (U.S.-requested) on escalating Ethiopia–Eritrea tensions after Addis and Asmara traded letters accusing each other of aggression. Ethiopian federal forces and allies entered Adwa without a fight after rebel withdrawal, following earlier gains at Mekelle and Adigrat—putting troops roughly 40 km from the Eritrean border as mediators warn of a wider Horn war.

Asia. After Monday’s North Korean ballistic launches toward the East Sea, Seoul, Washington, and Tokyo held Tuesday phone consultations on responses; Japan, the U.S., and South Korea urged Pyongyang to halt provocations. KCNA called the tactical test a “big success.” Taiwan tracked five PLA aircraft, six PLAN ships, and four official ships around the island overnight (four aircraft crossed the median line into the ADIZ).

Europe. Drones struck two merchant ships in Bulgaria’s Black Sea EEZ Tuesday, sinking one (Dignity) and prompting rescues; PM Radev summoned Russia’s ambassador and convened an emergency Security Council. Separately, all 27 EU states agreed to open accession Clusters 2 and 3 for Ukraine and Moldova after Hungary lifted its veto—formal opening framed for Tuesday.

North America. Hurricane Simon continued to batter western Mexico after related tropical systems killed at least five (including deaths tied to former Hurricane Rachel in Baja). Flood risk eased somewhat in the southwestern U.S. as authorities aired rescues and damage along Mexico’s Pacific coast.

South America. Brazil’s runoff campaign toward Oct. 25 intensified: Lula supporters rallied in Rio while Flávio Bolsonaro campaigned, and electoral-court justices clashed over a pro-Lula WhatsApp channel.

Oceania. Greater Sydney’s Monday total fire ban (extreme heat, dry-lightning risk) framed the overnight watch; New Zealand crews worked wind-driven hotspots at the contained Walter Peak vegetation fire near Queenstown.

beats.title: MAGA / MAHA promises kept
beats.headline: Diesel relief vs pump math; MAHA glyphosate backlash.
beats.body:
“Lower energy costs” — diesel tax relief & Russian diesel. Promise: Trump campaigned on cheaper fuel and ending wars fast. What was done: An October emergency order defers federal diesel excise-tax payments and eases highway use of tax-free dyed diesel through year-end, while he announced Russian diesel volumes and Treasury authorization for related transactions. Impact: Analysts (Forbes, CBS) say the volumes and logistics are unlikely to move U.S. pump prices much before midterms; Congress from both parties criticized buying Russian diesel amid the Ukraine war. The claimed Russia–Ukraine “energy ceasefire” still lacks Moscow confirmation and did not stop strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure.

“Take on Big Ag / cut toxins” — MAHA glyphosate ledger. Promise: RFK Jr. and MAHA vowed to confront pesticides and corporate capture of food and health. What was done: The administration expanded glyphosate production and advanced liability shields; a MAHA scorecard of dozens of pledges still shows few fully kept. Impact: An Oct. 13 ABC report details MAHA activists turning on Trump and Kennedy over broken glyphosate/pesticide promises, with open letters warning midterms and some voters saying their ballots are now up for grabs—while vaccine-advisory shakeups remain the clearest health-agency action delivered.

beats.title: Musk world
beats.headline: CRS-35 up; NHTSA Robotaxi school-zone review.
beats.body:
SpaceX — CRS-35. Falcon 9 lofted Cargo Dragon CRS-35 at 6:33 a.m. ET from Cape Canaveral SLC-40 with more than 6,300 pounds of cargo including the final ISS roll-out solar arrays; booster return targeted LZ-40. Docking still framed Thursday ~11 a.m. ET. Stockholder-relevant: another on-time NASA cargo flight and RTLS attempt on a high-flight core.

Tesla — Robotaxi scrutiny. NHTSA’s defect-petition review (DP26010) over alleged school-zone speeding by 2026 Model Y robotaxis and Cybercabs remains open—about 1,000 vehicles possibly affected, no crashes cited, ~120 days to grant or deny a formal probe. Quiet overnight beyond Monday’s Terafab / Starship ship-catch window notes.

beats.title: Space
beats.headline: CRS-35 aloft; Amazon Leo near service; Blue Origin pad.
beats.body:
Commercial LEO cargo. SpaceX’s CRS-35 success this morning (see NASA) is the day’s clearest industry milestone—final iROSA pair plus science headed to station.

Amazon Leo. Amazon has built its 1,000th Leo satellite and still targets commercial service before year-end, with hundreds already on orbit; next rides depend on Vulcan and other providers while Blue Origin’s New Glenn remains grounded.

Blue Origin. LC-36 rebuild work continues toward a hoped December New Glenn return; Bezos’s company keeps expanding in Texas amid IPO talk. Quiet otherwise on Monday’s Hutto Constellation Park notes.

beats.title: NASA
beats.headline: CRS-35 launched 6:33 a.m. ET; docking Thursday.
beats.body: SpaceX CRS-35 lifted off on time at 6:33 a.m. ET Tuesday from Cape Canaveral SLC-40—Falcon 9 / Dragon C211 with more than 6,300 pounds of cargo, including the final pair of ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays, science (artificial retinas, 3D heart tissue, glass, neurodegeneration organoids), and Canadarm2-return hardware. Autonomous docking still targeted Thursday, Oct. 15, around 11 a.m. ET at Harmony’s zenith port; splashdown return mid-November. Quiet otherwise on Friday’s Commercial LEO Destinations RFP.

beats.title: Catholic
beats.headline: Acutis expo continues; Pope at Gemelli; Tagle closes Amoris.
beats.body:
Miami. The St. Carlo Acutis Eucharistic Miracles Exposition continues at St. Mark the Evangelist (Southwest Ranches) this week. Corpus Christi Parish inaugurated Florida’s first marble statue of St. Carlo last night (Youth Group One project). No new Archdiocese clergy bulletin overnight.

United States / Latin America. Monday’s Holy See moves still stand: Fr. Milad Yaghi, M.L.M. (Houston pastor) named Maronite bishop for Mexico; Archbishop Ozoria Acosta’s Santo Domingo resignation accepted, with Coadjutor Morel Diplán succeeding.

Europe / Universal Church. Pope Leo’s Gemelli admission and afternoon lung-nodule surgery dominate the day (see World); Cardinal Tagle—newly noted as Dean of the College of Cardinals—presides Wednesday’s Amoris Laetitia tenth-anniversary closing Mass in the Pope’s stead. Quiet on fresh Africa/Asia/Oceania episcopal headlines beyond the weekend Italy/curia notes already briefed.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Countdown still Oct. 3; Medjugorje peace Rosary; France baptisms.
beats.body:
Countdown to the Kingdom. Rechecked this morning: nothing newer than Oct. 3—Marija’s “Time of Prayer for Peace,” Elizabeth Kindelmann (“Satan Will be Blinded”), and Pedro Regis (“Humanity is Sick”).

Latest Marian message. Our Lady’s Sept. 25 Medjugorje message through Marija remains the newest monthly message—calling families to renew the Rosary for peace so she may intercede before the Most High. October’s 25th message is not out yet.

Eucharistic signs / returns. Miami’s Acutis exposition and new marble statue (see Catholic) keep a local pilgrimage of documented Eucharistic miracles in view. France’s adult- and youth-baptism surge remains the clearest large-scale return-to-faith story. No sober new chip/digital-ID headline overnight worth elevating.

beats.body:
Today: Free family concert “Music from the Andes” at NSU’s Alvin Sherman Library in Sunrise (about 6–6:45 p.m.; ages 4+ welcome; pre-register if you can). Acutis Eucharistic Miracles Exposition continues at St. Mark, Southwest Ranches.

This week: Heat host Brooklyn Wednesday at Kaseya Center (7:30 p.m. ET tip)—see Pick-me-up. Miami-Dade library storytimes remain easy midweek family options. Bethel Music’s Fillmore show is done (Sunday).

beats.title: Pick-me-up
beats.headline: Heat host Nets Wednesday; Galactic Racer still humming.
beats.body: Heat still ride the 125–124 preseason heartbreaker to Minnesota into Wednesday’s home look at Brooklyn (7:30 p.m. ET, Kaseya Center), then at Orlando Oct. 16 to close preseason. On the Star Wars side, Galactic Racer (PS5, Xbox, PC; free for Prime on Luna) remains the week’s bright arcade hit more than a week after launch, with Sebulba and Crait still featured in the launch trailer—and Lucasfilm’s Ahsoka Season 2 still aimed at January 20, 2027.
